principles.name: Perceivable
principles.description: Information and user interface components must be presentable to users in ways they can perceive.

principles.name: Operable
principles.description: User interface components and navigation must be operable.

principles.name: Understandable
principles.description: Information and the operation of user interface must be understandable.

principles.name: Robust
principles.description: Content must be robust enough that it can be interpreted reliably by a wide variety of user agents, including assistive technologies.

criteria.name: Non-text Content
criteria.description: All non-text content that is presented to the user has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose, except for specific situations.
tests: Decorative images have empty alt or role=presentation

criteria.name: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
criteria.description: For prerecorded audio-only and prerecorded video-only media, provide an alternative.
tests: Video has text description or audio track

criteria.name: Captions (Prerecorded)
criteria.description: Captions are provided for all prerecorded audio content in synchronized media.

criteria.name: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
criteria.description: An alternative for time-based media or audio description is provided for prerecorded video content.
tests: Video has audio description or text alternative

criteria.name: Captions (Live)
criteria.description: Captions are provided for all live audio content in synchronized media.

criteria.name: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
criteria.description: Audio description is provided for all prerecorded video content.

criteria.name: Sign Language (Prerecorded)
criteria.description: Sign language interpretation is provided for all prerecorded audio content.

criteria.name: Extended Audio Description (Prerecorded)
criteria.description: Extended audio description is provided for all prerecorded video content where pauses are insufficient.
tests: Video pauses for extended audio description when needed

criteria.name: Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
criteria.description: An alternative for time-based media is provided for all prerecorded synchronized media and video-only media.
tests: Full text alternative provided for video

criteria.name: Audio-only (Live)
criteria.description: An alternative for time-based media is provided for all live audio-only content.
tests: Live audio has real-time text alternative

criteria.name: Info and Relationships
criteria.description: Information, structure, and relationships conveyed through presentation can be programmatically determined or are available in text.

criteria.name: Meaningful Sequence
criteria.description: When the sequence in which content is presented affects its meaning, a correct reading sequence can be programmatically determined.
tests: CSS positioning doesn't break reading order

criteria.name: Sensory Characteristics
criteria.description: Instructions do not rely solely on sensory characteristics such as shape, color, size, visual location, orientation, or sound.
tests: Instructions don't rely only on color
Instructions don't rely only on shape or location

criteria.name: Orientation
criteria.description: Content does not restrict its view and operation to a single display orientation unless essential.
tests: Content works in portrait and landscape

criteria.name: Identify Input Purpose
criteria.description: The purpose of each input field collecting information about the user can be programmatically determined.
tests: Personal data fields have appropriate autocomplete values

criteria.name: Identify Purpose
criteria.description: The purpose of user interface components, icons, and regions can be programmatically determined.

criteria.name: Use of Color
criteria.description: Color is not used as the only visual means of conveying information, indicating an action, prompting a response, or distinguishing a visual element.
tests: Form errors not indicated by color alone
Charts use patterns in addition to color

criteria.name: Audio Control
criteria.description: If any audio on a Web page plays automatically for more than 3 seconds, a mechanism is available to pause/stop or control volume.

criteria.name: Contrast (Minimum)
criteria.description: Text and images of text have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, except for large text (3:1), incidental text, and logotypes.
tests: Large text (18pt or 14pt bold) has 3:1 contrast

criteria.name: Resize Text
criteria.description: Text can be resized without assistive technology up to 200 percent without loss of content or functionality.

criteria.name: Images of Text
criteria.description: If the technologies being used can achieve the visual presentation, text is used rather than images of text.
tests: Text used instead of images of text

criteria.name: Contrast (Enhanced)
criteria.description: Text and images of text have a contrast ratio of at least 7:1, except for large text (4.5:1), incidental text, and logotypes.

criteria.name: Low or No Background Audio
criteria.description: For prerecorded audio-only content with primarily speech, background sounds are at least 20 dB lower than foreground speech.

criteria.name: Visual Presentation
criteria.description: For visual presentation of blocks of text, a mechanism is available to select foreground/background colors, width, line spacing, and text alignment.
tests: Paragraph spacing at least 2x line spacing

criteria.name: Images of Text (No Exception)
criteria.description: Images of text are only used for pure decoration or where a particular presentation is essential.
tests: No images of text except decoration

criteria.name: Reflow
criteria.description: Content can be presented without loss of information or functionality, and without requiring scrolling in two dimensions at 320 CSS pixels wide or 256 CSS pixels tall.
tests: No vertical scroll at 256px height for horizontal content

criteria.name: Non-text Contrast
criteria.description: Visual information required to identify UI components and graphical objects has a contrast ratio of at least 3:1.

criteria.name: Text Spacing
criteria.description: No loss of content or functionality when adjusting line height to 1.5x, paragraph spacing to 2x, letter spacing to 0.12x, and word spacing to 0.16x font size.
tests: Content readable with increased text spacing

criteria.name: Content on Hover or Focus
criteria.description: Where hover or focus triggers additional content to appear, the additional content is dismissible, hoverable, and persistent.
tests: Pointer can move to hover content

criteria.name: Keyboard
criteria.description: All functionality is operable through a keyboard interface without requiring specific timings for individual keystrokes.

criteria.name: No Keyboard Trap
criteria.description: If keyboard focus can be moved to a component, focus can be moved away using only a keyboard.
tests: Can Tab out of all components
Modal dialogs trap focus appropriately but allow escape

criteria.name: Keyboard (No Exception)
criteria.description: All functionality is operable through a keyboard interface without exception.
tests: All functionality keyboard accessible including path-dependent input

criteria.name: Character Key Shortcuts
criteria.description: If a keyboard shortcut uses only letter, punctuation, number, or symbol characters, it can be turned off, remapped, or is only active on focus.
tests: Shortcuts only active when component focused

criteria.name: Timing Adjustable
criteria.description: For each time limit, at least one of the following is true: turn off, adjust, extend, or the time limit is essential/real-time/20+ hours.

criteria.name: Pause, Stop, Hide
criteria.description: For moving, blinking, scrolling, or auto-updating information, there is a mechanism to pause, stop, or hide.

criteria.name: No Timing
criteria.description: Timing is not an essential part of the event or activity, except for non-interactive synchronized media and real-time events.

criteria.name: Interruptions
criteria.description: Interruptions can be postponed or suppressed by the user, except for emergencies.

criteria.name: Re-authenticating
criteria.description: When an authenticated session expires, the user can continue without loss of data after re-authenticating.

criteria.name: Timeouts
criteria.description: Users are warned of the duration of any user inactivity that could cause data loss, unless data is preserved for more than 20 hours.

criteria.name: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
criteria.description: Web pages do not contain anything that flashes more than three times in any one second period, or the flash is below general and red flash thresholds.
tests: No content flashes more than 3 times per second

criteria.name: Three Flashes
criteria.description: Web pages do not contain anything that flashes more than three times in any one second period.
tests: No content flashes more than 3 times per second

criteria.name: Animation from Interactions
criteria.description: Motion animation triggered by interaction can be disabled, unless essential.

criteria.name: Bypass Blocks
criteria.description: A mechanism is available to bypass blocks of content that are repeated on multiple Web pages.

criteria.name: Page Titled
criteria.description: Web pages have titles that describe topic or purpose.

criteria.name: Focus Order
criteria.description: If a Web page can be navigated sequentially and navigation sequences affect meaning or operation, focusable components receive focus in an order that preserves meaning and operability.

criteria.name: Link Purpose (In Context)
criteria.description: The purpose of each link can be determined from the link text alone or from the link text together with its programmatically determined context.
tests: Links with same text go to same destination

criteria.name: Multiple Ways
criteria.description: More than one way is available to locate a Web page within a set of Web pages, except where the page is a result of or step in a process.

criteria.name: Headings and Labels
criteria.description: Headings and labels describe topic or purpose.

criteria.name: Focus Visible
criteria.description: Any keyboard operable user interface has a mode of operation where the keyboard focus indicator is visible.

criteria.name: Location
criteria.description: Information about the user's location within a set of Web pages is available.

criteria.name: Link Purpose (Link Only)
criteria.description: A mechanism is available to allow the purpose of each link to be identified from link text alone.

criteria.name: Section Headings
criteria.description: Section headings are used to organize the content.

criteria.name: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
criteria.description: When a user interface component receives keyboard focus, the component is not entirely hidden by author-created content.
tests: Focused element at least partially visible

criteria.name: Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced)
criteria.description: When a user interface component receives keyboard focus, no part of the component is hidden by author-created content.

criteria.name: Focus Appearance
criteria.description: When keyboard focus indicator is visible, the focus indicator area is at least as large as a 2 CSS pixel thick perimeter and has 3:1 contrast against unfocused state.
tests: Focus indicator at least 2px thick perimeter

criteria.name: Pointer Gestures
criteria.description: All functionality that uses multipoint or path-based gestures can be operated with a single pointer without a path-based gesture.

criteria.name: Pointer Cancellation
criteria.description: For single pointer functionality, at least one of the following is true: no down-event, abort/undo, up reversal, or essential.

criteria.name: Label in Name
criteria.description: For UI components with labels that include text or images of text, the accessible name contains the text that is presented visually.

criteria.name: Motion Actuation
criteria.description: Functionality operated by device motion or user motion can also be operated by UI components and response to motion can be disabled.

criteria.name: Target Size (Enhanced)
criteria.description: The size of the target for pointer inputs is at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels.
tests: Touch targets at least 44x44 CSS pixels

criteria.name: Concurrent Input Mechanisms
criteria.description: Web content does not restrict use of input modalities available on a platform except where the restriction is essential or required for security.
tests: Can use keyboard, mouse, touch interchangeably

criteria.name: Dragging Movements
criteria.description: All functionality that uses a dragging movement can be achieved by a single pointer without dragging, unless dragging is essential.

criteria.name: Target Size (Minimum)
criteria.description: The size of the target for pointer inputs is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, with exceptions for inline targets, user agent control, essential sizing, and spacing.
tests: Touch targets at least 24x24 CSS pixels or have sufficient spacing

criteria.name: Language of Page
criteria.description: The default human language of each Web page can be programmatically determined.

criteria.name: Language of Parts
criteria.description: The human language of each passage or phrase in the content can be programmatically determined except for proper names, technical terms, words of indeterminate language, and words that have become part of the vernacular.
tests: Foreign phrases marked with lang attribute

criteria.name: Unusual Words
criteria.description: A mechanism is available for identifying specific definitions of words or phrases used in an unusual or restricted way.

criteria.name: Abbreviations
criteria.description: A mechanism for identifying the expanded form or meaning of abbreviations is available.

criteria.name: Reading Level
criteria.description: When text requires reading ability more advanced than lower secondary education level, supplemental content or a version at that level is available.
tests: Content readable at lower secondary level

criteria.name: Pronunciation
criteria.description: A mechanism is available for identifying specific pronunciation of words where meaning is ambiguous without knowing pronunciation.

criteria.name: On Focus
criteria.description: When any user interface component receives focus, it does not initiate a change of context.

criteria.name: On Input
criteria.description: Changing the setting of any user interface component does not automatically cause a change of context unless the user has been advised beforehand.

criteria.name: Consistent Navigation
criteria.description: Navigational mechanisms that are repeated on multiple Web pages within a set occur in the same relative order each time.

criteria.name: Consistent Identification
criteria.description: Components that have the same functionality within a set of Web pages are identified consistently.
tests: Same function has same label across site

criteria.name: Change on Request
criteria.description: Changes of context are initiated only by user request or a mechanism is available to turn off such changes.

criteria.name: Consistent Help
criteria.description: If a Web page contains help mechanisms they occur in the same relative order on each page.

criteria.name: Error Identification
criteria.description: If an input error is automatically detected, the item that is in error is identified and the error is described to the user in text.
tests: Error not indicated by color alone

criteria.name: Labels or Instructions
criteria.description: Labels or instructions are provided when content requires user input.

criteria.name: Error Suggestion
criteria.description: If an input error is detected and suggestions for correction are known, they are provided to the user unless it would jeopardize security or purpose.

criteria.name: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
criteria.description: For legal commitments, financial transactions, or user-controllable data: submissions are reversible, data is checked with opportunity to correct, or a confirmation mechanism is provided.
tests: Data can be reviewed before submit

criteria.name: Help
criteria.description: Context-sensitive help is available.
tests: Help text available for complex forms

criteria.name: Error Prevention (All)
criteria.description: For all forms that require user submission: submissions are reversible, data is checked with opportunity to correct, or confirmation is provided.
tests: All forms have confirmation or undo

criteria.name: Redundant Entry
criteria.description: Information previously entered or provided that is required to be entered again in the same process is either auto-populated or available for selection.

criteria.name: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
criteria.description: A cognitive function test is not required for any step in an authentication process unless an alternative, mechanism, or object recognition is provided.

criteria.name: Accessible Authentication (Enhanced)
criteria.description: A cognitive function test is not required for any step in an authentication process.
tests: No cognitive tests for authentication at all

criteria.name: Parsing
criteria.description: In content implemented using markup languages, elements have complete start and end tags, are nested according to specifications, do not contain duplicate attributes, and IDs are unique.

criteria.name: Name, Role, Value
criteria.description: For all user interface components, the name and role can be programmatically determined; states, properties, and values that can be set by the user can be programmatically set; and notification of changes is available to user agents.

criteria.name: Status Messages
criteria.description: In content implemented using markup languages, status messages can be programmatically determined through role or properties such that they can be presented to the user by assistive technologies without receiving focus.
